notes: claim 48: severity major on a rationale: risk rating lowered to minor; ratings are judgements and cannot hold a page
claim 49: severity blocker on a rationale: impact rating lowered to minor; ratings are judgements and cannot hold a page
summary: Hold: the briefing treats the billing page's entitlement as consumption-based, although the sources establish metered usage, not the licence needed to access this page. It also asserts an exclusive viewing audience despite acknowledging that viewing roles are unpublished. The existing licence-assignment and report-privacy controls are supported.

claims.claim: The report privacy checkbox is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Org settings > Services > Reports > Conceal user, group, and site names in all reports.
claims.quote: Select Org Settings. ... On the Services tab, select Reports. ... In the Reports panel, uncheck the checkbox next to Conceal user, group, and site names in all reports.

claims.claim: PATCH /v1.0/admin/reportSettings sets report privacy through the displayConcealedNames request-body property.
claims.quote: PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/admin/reportSettings ... displayConcealedNames ... If set to true, all reports conceal user information such as usernames, groups, and sites. If false, all reports show identifiable information.

claims.claim: The usage-report privacy setting applies to the Credits report.
claims.quote: By default, user-specific information like usernames, display names, groups, and sites is hidden in usage reports. To learn how to display this information in usage reports, see Show user, group, or site details in usage reports.
